evals.name: choose-shop-strategies-and-entropy
evals.prompt: On Screenplay 4.151.0, our shop has CustomerId (cus_ plus ULID), OrderId (TypeID) and InviteCode (NanoID). Show their concept generation declarations and a generated CustomerId command property. A shorter InviteCode proposal uses 16 hexadecimal symbols; compute its random bits versus the default NanoID. Does the customer prefix add entropy or guarantee ordering? We also have ApiKey from .NET Bytes(32) with NotAudited and an Arc context-aware OrderId. Which parts can Screenplay execute today? Separately, on 6.32.0 DispatchConsignments has runId String identifier and consignmentIds String[]. Its resolved C# handler must emit one RunOpened and zero or more ConsignmentDispatched, in returned order, choosing among consignmentIds. Show the handler contract and explain a PLAY0800 after emptying its attached body. A teammate says may produce always fails binding and wants produces ... when instead. Correct them without promising standalone execution. Reply only; no tools or edits.
evals.expected_output: CustomerId is String with generate ulid prefix "cus_"; OrderId uses generate typeid "order"; InviteCode uses generate nanoid. The command property is customerId CustomerId generated identifier, with no per-property strategy. Default NanoID has 126 bits; 16 positions in a 16-symbol alphabet have 64 bits, meeting the identifier floor. Prefixes add none; time order is not monotonic within a millisecond. Preserve ApiKey secret but do not generate it; received-time/tenant context and secret execution remain Screenplay#616 phases 3/4. The ordinary TypeID strategy is not equivalent to Arc's context contract. Separate source, executable and target gates. On 6.32.0 use handler may produce with RunOpened for runId and ConsignmentDispatched for one of consignmentIds, plus a resolved nonempty language-tagged body. Result v2/ESM v35 binds from 5.4.0 (syntax 4.256.0, provider seam 4.257.0); an ordered subset/multiset permits zero/repeated items, not simultaneous produces. Conditional produces and attached empty/unresolved bodies still fail PLAY0800: inspect code/arguments.subject, restore the body or choose unconditional productions/split commands. No body or implementation declaration is an invalid set (PLAY0823); pending v2 is described intent, while pending v1 has distinct PLAY0696/0697. Required scalar destinations permit generation only for identifiers; one-of requires a non-generated collection. The standalone runner has no provider.
assertions: Places ULID/cus_, TypeID/order and NanoID strategies on String concepts and generated identifier on the command property.
Computes 64 random bits for the custom InviteCode and 126 for default NanoID, adds no prefix entropy and rejects strict within-millisecond ordering.
Preserves ApiKey secret classification without claiming executable secret generation, and distinguishes TypeID shape from Arc receipt-time/tenant context.
Separates authoring, binding/reference execution and target support; does not call entropy evidence an executable or render verdict.

Shows scalar and one-of may produce destinations with a resolved body, version-gates v35/v2 binding, rejects simultaneous/conditional produces, and repairs PLAY0800 from structured diagnostics without calling standalone body execution supported.

evals.name: refuse-gapless-invoice-generation
evals.prompt: Our shop's Screenplay 4.151.0 billing model needs legally gapless invoice numbers shared across concurrent commands. Can generate sequence, random numbers with retries, generate pattern with a date, or generate rule reading the previous invoice solve it today? We also receive a client-minted CustomerId and a webhook idempotency key. Reply only with what to model or leave open, without inventing allocator APIs.
evals.expected_output: None is a released gapless allocator. generate sequence is reserved (PLAY0682); pattern/random/rule parse but refuse executable binding (PLAY0268), and read-then-write plus randomness cannot enforce gapless concurrent allocation. Keep the allocator requirement as an explicit capability gap/owning implementation question (Screenplay#619). CustomerId remains an input; idempotency needs a persisted/deterministic request mapping with independent uniqueness, not new randomness or a future derive promise.
assertions: Refuses randomness, retries and read-then-write as a gapless concurrent invoice allocator.
Names sequence as reserved and pattern/random/rule as non-executable, not shipped solutions.
Preserves the business requirement as an explicit capability gap without inventing a sequence or derive API.
Keeps client-minted CustomerId as input and treats idempotency/uniqueness independently of generation.

evals.name: generation-is-not-protection
evals.prompt: RegisterCustomer on Screenplay 4.151.0 has a cus_-prefixed ULID generated identifier. A teammate wants it as ApiKey, removes authorization and adds a generated-concept matches rule based on high entropy; executable.status is notAssessed due to another declaration's binding error. Assess that historical case. Separately, on 6.15.0, expose Sales.Invoices.Creating.Create to agents with read scope and approval required, then remove inherited Staff authorization because approvalRequired is false. Another public command must stay unexposed. What do we declare or refuse? Reply only; no tools/edits.
evals.expected_output: In the 4.151.0 case, a time-visible CustomerId is not a credential or authorization; retain policy and ApiKey secret classification. Secret generation and generated-concept validation/rule consistency are unadmitted there. High entropy proves neither security nor binding; notAssessed is unknown, inspect diagnostics and reassess after scoped repair without fabricated regex/checksum/proof repairs. For 6.15.0/ESM v48, route to toolchain agent-exposure/manifest references: root agents, tokens personal, command Sales.Invoices.Creating.Create with scope write and a nonempty literal description. Public/unlisted commands remain default-deny; retain effective Staff authorization. Read-scoped commands refuse PLAY0971; approval required PLAY0974 and approve PLAY0964 are unsupported. approvalRequired false bypasses neither token scope nor authorization. No automatic analyzer or Arc configuration claim.
assertions: Rejects CustomerId as ApiKey and retains authorization/secret classification; historical 4.151.0 secrets and generated-concept validation/rule consistency stay unadmitted without invented repairs.
Treats notAssessed as unknown and entropy as neither security nor whole-model binding; inspects diagnostics before reassessment.
Routes to toolchain with 6.15.0/ESM v48 and declares root agents/personal tokens, exact command, write scope and literal description; unlisted public commands stay unexposed.
Refuses command read scope PLAY0971, approval required PLAY0974 and approve PLAY0964 instead of silently deleting the boundary.
Keeps inherited authorization and token scope despite approvalRequired false; invents neither Arc configuration nor automatic comparison.

evals.name: readable-invoice-pattern-not-gapless-sequence
evals.prompt: Use Screenplay 4.199.0 for a shop: OrderId is a TypeID generated identifier; InvoiceNumber must read INV-UTCyearmonth-sevenrandomdigits plus Luhn check digit; pickupTicket is a six-digit random Int. Show concept syntax, generated value pins and a clock. Should a unique constraint cover the short payload codes? Does this provide legally gapless numbering, secrecy, or Stage rendering? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: InvoiceNumber String declares generate pattern "INV-{yyyy}{MM}-#{7}" checksum luhn and validate checksum luhn; TicketNumber Int declares generate random 100000..999999. Keep those generated values separate from OrderId generated identifier; pin whole OrderId with for, named generated invoiceNumber = "INV-202610-00000004" and integral pickupTicket with given clock "2026-10-02T09:00:00Z". Pattern/random/checksum select v21, require 4.172.0 and bind/reference-execute with fixtures, not PLAY0268. Short payloads need single-property uniqueness; source freshness is separate. Dates/check digits add no entropy. Not gapless/sequential, not a secret, check digits catch typos not forgery. Stage requires 4.118.0 for checksum validation and 4.119.0 for pattern/random; generate rule remains STAGE-ESM-028. Sequence and generated secrets remain refused.
assertions: Shows concept-owned pattern with checksum plus separate validate checksum and inclusive Int random range, not a per-property strategy or Int identifier.
Pins whole identifiers and named values with a UTC clock; dates match that instant, and the numeric fixture is not quoted.
Explains exact support/entropy excludes dates and check digits, short payload uniqueness and whole-source freshness serve different roles, and generation never silently retries.
Separates v21 reference admission from Stage rendering and refuses pattern for gapless sequences, credentials or authorization; checksums detect typos not forgery.

evals.name: repair-refuted-generated-concept-rule
evals.prompt: On Screenplay 4.199.0, InviteCode uses generate nanoid but validates matches ^[0-9]{21}$. Compilation reports PLAY0688 with a letter-containing witness; MCP provides derivedPattern and the rule has diagnosticCode and repair PLAY0688. How should we fix this if the NanoID strategy is intended? What if a different rule is unproven? Can a renderer use RuleConsistency.Check? Separately on Screenplay 6.32.0, InvoiceRegistered declares tag invoicing and its produces adds tag billing. Is this already a specification assertion? Show the corresponding then tag checks, contrast no tags and omission, preserve payload property tag = and for/routing checks, and say whether reference support proves Stage admission. Reply only; preserve input/stored-value consequences.
evals.expected_output: Read generation.rules[] and witness, obtain discovered repair subject and both revision guards, propose-repair PLAY0688 with canonical formatting, review input/stored-value validation changes, run proposal specs, then apply. A new rule can use derivedPattern through a typed matches proposal. Proven silent, Refuted error, Unproven PLAY0689 warning with reason; matches containment requires deterministic patterns, passing samples prove nothing. The 4.174.0 RuleConsistency.Check(SemanticConcept,int? utcAssessmentYear) API returns authored-order results including implicit UUID for generated properties. Capable renderers may allow unpinned all-Proven generation, Unproven needs pins; reference evaluator always pins. Stage 4.115.0 permits the all-Proven case; Unproven/Refuted rules still require pins (-038), invalid pins fail -011. Do not delete intended rules or retry generation. Declaration/production tags describe appends, not assertions. On 6.32.0/ESM v55 assert tag invoicing then tag billing under the then event, exact order/count; no tags means empty, omission unchecked. Preserve tag = payload and for/routing checks; reference support is not Stage renderer admission.
assertions: Reads structured rules/witness and proposes the discovered PLAY0688 repair with both revisions, never a text bypass or removal of the business rule.
Reviews the derived matches change as validation for supplied/stored values too and distinguishes adding a typed rule from replacing through repair.
Distinguishes silent Proven, Refuted error and Unproven warning with reason; passing samples and ambiguous regexes do not establish proof.
Names the renderer proof API and assessment year, differentiates capable-target all-Proven allowance from Unproven pins, reference pins and Stage's version-gated all-Proven allowance.

Distinguishes producer/declaration tags from then assertions; on 6.32.0/ESM v55 writes exact ordered invoicing/billing expectations, contrasts no tags with unchecked omission, preserves payload tag = and for/routing checks, and does not infer renderer admission.
